sources.entry: uuid-utils - A fast, Rust-backed drop-in replacement for Python's built-in uuid module.

summary.one_liner: A fast, Rust-powered drop-in replacement for Python's built-in uuid module, providing uuid1 through uuid8 generators.
summary.what_it_does: Provides Python functions for generating UUIDs of versions 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, implemented in Rust. Versions 3 and 5 hash a namespace UUID and a name (MD5 and SHA-1 respectively), version 4 uses random data, version 7 uses a Unix timestamp so values sort by time, and version 8 takes user-defined data. The README says it can be used in place of the standard uuid module. A separate uuid_utils.compat module returns standard-library uuid.UUID instances for frameworks such as Django that require them. The README includes a benchmark run on macOS with Python 3.14 showing uuid4 and uuid7 generation, and from_hex and from_bytes parsing, several times faster than the stdlib in its own tests.
use_cases: deterministic UUIDs from names via namespace hashing
speeding up UUID creation in Python code
parsing UUIDs from hex or bytes quickly
using UUIDs with Django that need stdlib UUID objects
how_to_run: import uuid_utils.compat as uuid  # returns stdlib uuid.UUID objects
make build && make test  # local development
notable: Drop-in replacement API for Python's uuid module
uuid_utils.compat returns stdlib uuid.UUID instances for frameworks like Django
Benchmarks in README show several-fold speedups over stdlib on Apple M3 Pro
caveats: Benchmark numbers come from a single macOS Apple M3 Pro run and may differ elsewhere
Default uuid_utils objects are a custom subclass, so code needing stdlib uuid.UUID must use the compat module
Local development requires building the Rust extension with make or maturin
